Single-cell deconvolution of one bulk sample

Source: R/02_02_single_cell_decovart_estimate_ratios.R
deconvolute_single_cell.Rd

Fits one bulk sample from the linear single-cell mixture \(\boldsymbol{y}\sim\mathcal{N}(c\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}\boldsymbol{p}, \phi\boldsymbol{S}_W(\boldsymbol{p}))\).

The start is single_cell_nuisance_scales(): nonnegative least squares with a free scale (DeconRNASeq's quadratic programme without the simplex equality), then the closed-form scales at that composition.

With profile = TRUE (default) the two scales are profiled out: for every trial composition they are recomputed in closed form, so the weight matrix \(\boldsymbol{S}_W(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1}\) is rebuilt at every iterate, and Newton-Raphson runs on the profile log-likelihood of the \(J-1\) ILR coordinates (profile_loglik_single_cell_ilr()). Its limit is the joint maximum-likelihood estimate of \((\boldsymbol{p},c,\phi)\), reached in one loop.

With profile = FALSE the scales stay at their start values (a two-stage plug-in fit), which is not the joint maximum. Supplying both mean_scale and variance_scale fixes them at those values.

With optimiser = "newton" (default) every fit uses the analytic score and observed Hessian with the PORT trust region of stats::nlminb(): the step maximises the quadratic model inside a ball whose radius grows or shrinks with the ratio of actual to predicted increase; there is no line search and no fixed step length. With optimiser = "lbfgsb" the same objective is maximised by L-BFGS-B on the closure \(\boldsymbol{p}=\boldsymbol{w}/\mathbf{1}^{\top} \boldsymbol{w}\), \(\boldsymbol{w}\ge0\), as in deconvolute_ratios_L_BFGS_B(); it can return exact zeros, where rho and the covariances are NA. The returned vcov is the delta-method image of the inverse negative profile Hessian; intervals are confint_single_cell().

Usage

deconvolute_single_cell(
  y,
  mean_signature_matrix,
  Sigma,
  epsilon = 1e-08,
  itmax = 100L,
  profile = TRUE,
  initial_p = NULL,
  mean_scale = NULL,
  variance_scale = NULL,
  estimand = c("cellular", "transcript"),
  cell_size = NULL,
  optimiser = c("newton", "lbfgsb")
)

Arguments

y

Bulk vector of length \(G\).

mean_signature_matrix

Reference mean, \(G\times J\).

Sigma

Cell-level covariances, \(G\times G\times J\).

epsilon

Relative function and step tolerances passed to stats::nlminb().

itmax

Maximum number of iterations.

profile

If TRUE, profile the two scales out; if FALSE, keep them at their start values.

initial_p

Optional open-simplex start. NULL uses the free-scale least-squares start.

mean_scale, variance_scale

Optional fixed scales. Supply both or neither.

estimand

cellular (default) interprets the fitted composition as a cell fraction, which is valid when the mean keeps the cell sizes \(S_j\). transcript interprets it as a transcript fraction; pass cell_size to convert it back to a cell fraction.

cell_size

Optional \(S_j\). Defaults to the column sums of the mean, which equal the cell sizes for a cellular_raw reference.

optimiser

"newton" (trust-region Newton in ILR coordinates) or "lbfgsb" (L-BFGS-B on the closed simplex).

Value

A list with composition (the fitted simplex coordinate), p, q, rho, estimand, fit_type ("profile", "two_stage" or "fixed_scales"), mean_scale, variance_scale, platform_scale, n_cells, cell_size, ols_scale, loglik, convergence (0 from stats::nlminb() means success), iterations, p_start, message, vcov_rho, vcov and vcov_nuisance (see vcov_single_cell()). A singular information matrix is returned as NA without failing the fit.

See also

single_cell_nuisance_scales(), profile_loglik_single_cell_ilr(), deconvolute_ratios_Newton_Raphson(), rescale_single_cell_moments()

Examples

genes <- paste0("g", 1:4)
cts <- paste0("ct", 1:2)
mu <- matrix(
  c(2, 2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 3, 3),
  nrow = 4,
  dimnames = list(genes, cts)
)
sigma <- array(0, c(4, 4, 2), dimnames = list(genes, genes, cts))
sigma[,, 1] <- diag(0.05, 4)
sigma[,, 2] <- diag(0.05, 4)
set.seed(1)
sim <- simulate_bulk_from_cells(
  mu,
  sigma,
  p = c(0.8, 0.2),
  n_cells = 2000,
  platform_scale = 1
)
fit <- deconvolute_single_cell(sim$Y[, 1], mu, sigma)
round(fit$p, 3)
#>   ct1   ct2 
#> 0.801 0.199
